subject: atlantic cod
title: Cod Ate 10 Million Fish in Hours, the Biggest Feast Ever Recorded

scenes.text: Twenty-three million fish banded together for safety. It backfired.
Off Norway, at sunrise, little fish called capelin crowded into one shoal over six miles long.
Scientists were watching from miles away, using sound waves.
Then two and a half million cod found them.
In just a few hours, the cod ate about ten and a half million capelin. The biggest predation event ever recorded.
And that whole shoal was only a tenth of one percent of the capelin spawning there.

description:
In February 2014, off northern Norway, about 23 million capelin formed one shoal more than 10 kilometres long. A shoal of about 2.5 million Atlantic cod then ate roughly 10.5 million of them within a few hours.
MIT researchers reconstructed it from ocean acoustic data, calling it the largest predation event ever observed.
Would you rather be the cod or the capelin?
first_comment: The scientists say the capelin switched from swimming alone to moving as one wave once they got crowded enough. Is safety in numbers a myth?
